sanity_expectations: M is finite and real over the whole B-T region
At fixed T, M increases monotonically with B and levels off (saturates) at large B
At weak field, M is nearly linear in B
At fixed B, M decreases with increasing T
The Schottky contribution is most pronounced at low T and high B
excitation_report: sigma=0.01, k=5. Per additive term (Sobol, 512 samples over B in [0.1,8], T in [2,50]): main Brillouin term 14.06*sigma; Curie impurity term 5.12*sigma (after scaling C_curie 0.05->0.11); Schottky term RMS 3.57*sigma but its PEAK effect (= new term E-parent) is 20.70*sigma, strongest at B~7.91, T~3.02, passes=true. The Schottky term is physically localized to the low-T/high-B corner (Schottky anomaly), hence low RMS but a strong peak well above 5*sigma. All terms are visible somewhere in the sampled region.
role_corrections: B: input/axis -> independent variable (confirmed, gets range [0.1,8] T; avoid B=0 where coth terms individually diverge though they cancel)
T: input/axis -> independent variable (confirmed, gets range [2,50] K)
mu: P -> P (confirmed, fixed to Bohr magneton 9.274e-24 J/T)
k_B: P -> P (confirmed, fixed to Boltzmann constant 1.380649e-23 J/K)
lambda_mf: P -> P (confirmed; kept << k_B*T so mean-field denominator stays positive)
C_curie: P -> P (confirmed; value raised for excitation)
Delta_cf: P -> P (confirmed, ~7 K gap within suggested 1e-23..1e-21 J)
rationale: Static algebraic relation solvable for M with no derivatives or integrals -> explicit, evaluate_explicit. B (field) and T (temperature) are the two independently-tuned experimental axes and get ranges; all other symbols are fixed constants. mu and k_B fixed to true physical constants; lambda_mf kept well below k_B*T so the mean-field denominator k_B*T - lambda_mf*N_sat*tanh(...) stays strictly positive (verified finite at both corners). Ranges chosen to span the weak-field linear regime through Brillouin saturation, and to include the low-T/high-B corner where the new Schottky term is strongest (peak 20.7*sigma).

scenario_text: A paramagnetic solid is placed in an external magnetic field at fixed temperature, and its net magnetization is measured. At weak fields the magnetization grows nearly linearly with field strength, but at strong fields it levels off as the microscopic moments become fully aligned. The experiment records magnetization as the field and temperature are independently tuned.
